description: IR emitted by #lang al. Generated from racket/al/private/vocab.rkt — do not edit.

items.description: (adw NAME … (steps STEP …)): an AI Developer Workflow. The four PITER choices default to the first declared option of each family.

changes.description: What the ADW changes. `codebase`: the application. `layer`: an agentic layer (its codebase is the repository that holds a layer, as in the workflow `al improve` runs); such an ADW never ships without a person and is exempt from the in-repo layer protection.

classes.description: Work classes routed to this ADW by classification; empty = any.

deliverTo.description: Stage this workflow delivers into; "" = the first stage that accepts the run's class. Only with declared stages.

pinnedHome.description: Only with a (placement …): why the workflow always runs on `home`, one sentence each; empty = it may run on any listed host.

oneOf.description: (run NAME #:command C …): one agent, one prompt, one purpose.

agent.description: Agent for this step only; empty = the ADW's agent. Use it for a cheaper model on routine steps or a different vendor for an independent step.

modelSet.description: Model tier for this step; `inherit` = the command's, unless the request names a tier (a task-file tag or issue keyword).

when.description: Run only for this work class.

oneOf.description: (check NAME #:cmd C …): a deterministic feedback loop. Runs a codebase command; on failure an agent resolves and the command re-runs. (check NAME #:cmds affected …) stands for one check step per codebase cmd that declares #:covers, each named after its cmd, with #:when-affected #t and the other fields as written.

forbidSkipReason.description: The check fails when a skipped test's reason contains this text (case-insensitive), e.g. "no podman"; "" = none. Skips without a visible reason then fail it too (pytest: -rs, go test: -v).

in.description: Environment option the command runs in, together with the ADW's worktree: a podman option (its own container, e.g. one with #:nested-engine #t) or a nix-devshell option (on the host). "" = the ADW's own environment stack. The gate's re-run of the same cmd runs there too.

maxSkipped.description: The check fails when more tests than this were skipped (counted from the output of pytest, go test, cargo test, mocha or a collected JUnit report); -1 = no limit. With a limit set, output al cannot count fails the check.

resolve.description: Command given the failing output; empty = fail the run immediately.

whenAffected.description: #t = the step runs its cmd only when the run's changed paths (against the run's base; in a review round, since the cmd last passed) touch the cmd's #:covers, or the cmd is #:always #t. Not run, it is recorded as not affected with the paths compared, never as passed. A layer change, a changed path no check of the workflow covers, and a changed file two #:always #f checks cover run it anyway.

oneOf.description: (script NAME #:cmd C …): run a declared codebase cmd as a workflow step, e.g. a workflow script the team already has. It runs in the run's environment (worktree, container), gets the run context in environment variables (ADW_ID, ADW_PROMPT, ADW_CLASS, ADW_PLAN, ADW_BRANCH, ADW_WORKTREE, ADW_LAYER_DIR, ADW_RESUME), its output becomes the step's output ($out.NAME), and a non-zero exit fails the run, unless the exit code is one of its #:waiting-exit codes: then the run ends as `waiting`, and `--resume` runs the step again with ADW_RESUME=1 (empty otherwise). It is not a check: no resolve loop, and the gate does not count it as verification.

args.description: Arguments appended to the command, each shell-quoted; $prompt, $plan, $adw_id, $class, $branch and $out.<step> are substituted.

journal.description: A folder the script writes its own run journal to, relative to the run's worktree; {adw_id} is the run id. While the script runs, each line of its events.jsonl is mirrored into the run's events (script.event) and each inner step's prompt.md and output files become documents of the run. A missing folder is not an error.

waitingExit.description: Exit codes that mean the script is waiting for something outside (e.g. 75): the run ends as `waiting` (not failed, not passed), keeps its worktree and prints how to resume; `--resume` runs this step again with ADW_RESUME=1.

oneOf.description: (review [NAME] …): run the ADW's review option here.

implement.description: Command/HOP that implements the patch plan.

patch.description: Command that plans a patch for a blocker; implemented via the ADW's implement command.

oneOf.description: (ship [NAME]): apply the review option's ship policy (PR / merge / deploy). Must come after a review step.

message.description: Extra text for the PR/merge message.

oneOf.description: (fan-out NAME #:adw CHILD …): run COUNT independent candidate runs of the child ADW (same prompt and class, each in its own worktree, branch, container and slots), pick a winner and merge its commits into this run's worktree, so later steps work on them. The child must commit its work and must not ship. Every candidate holds one `runs` slot and so does the parent: #:max-runs of (concurrency slots …) must exceed the number of concurrent parents plus candidates.

adw.description: The child ADW each candidate runs.

pick.description: `best`: of the passing candidates, the one with the fewest resolve attempts, then the smallest diff, then the earliest; `first`: the first to pass; `all`: every candidate must pass and all are merged in order.

agents.description: The coding agent a step runs on. ADWs name one; the runtime shells out to it headlessly. An agent offers named model tiers: `base` and `heavy` always exist (see #:model-base / #:model-heavy), and #:models adds any others. Commands, hops and run steps pick a tier with #:model-set.

oneOf.description: Claude Code in programmable mode (`claude -p`), stream-json output.

allowedTools.description: Tools the headless agent may use without asking (passed as --allowedTools). Narrow it for read-only workflows.

maxTurns.description: Turn cap per step (about two and a half hours of work at a usual pace).

models.description: Named model tiers, e.g. ((fast "claude-haiku-5-5") (heavy "claude-fable-5-2" #:effort high)). `base` and `heavy` may be given here instead of with #:model-base / #:model-heavy, but not both ways.

items.description: One model tier of an agent, written (TIER "MODEL-ID" [#:effort LEVEL]) inside #:models.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this tier: `default` leaves it to the CLI. Claude Code: passed as --effort (low…max). codex: passed as -c model_reasoning_effort=LEVEL (low…xhigh; codex has no flag of its own for it). Not available for custom agents.

model.description: Model id passed to the agent CLI.

tier.description: Tier name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes (not `inherit`).

permissionMode.description: Headless permission mode. bypassPermissions only inside a podman environment.

safeMode.description: Run with --safe-mode so user CLAUDE.md, hooks, plugins and skills are not loaded.

oneOf.description: OpenAI Codex CLI (`codex exec`). It reports no cost, so spending limits count its calls as $0.

items.description: One model tier of an agent, written (TIER "MODEL-ID" [#:effort LEVEL]) inside #:models.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this tier: `default` leaves it to the CLI. Claude Code: passed as --effort (low…max). codex: passed as -c model_reasoning_effort=LEVEL (low…xhigh; codex has no flag of its own for it). Not available for custom agents.

model.description: Model id passed to the agent CLI.

tier.description: Tier name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes (not `inherit`).

oneOf.description: Any CLI agent. The command receives the rendered prompt on stdin. It reports no cost, so spending limits count its calls as $0.

models.description: Named model tiers (see claude-code); #:effort is not available.

items.description: One model tier of an agent, written (TIER "MODEL-ID" [#:effort LEVEL]) inside #:models.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this tier: `default` leaves it to the CLI. Claude Code: passed as --effort (low…max). codex: passed as -c model_reasoning_effort=LEVEL (low…xhigh; codex has no flag of its own for it). Not available for custom agents.

model.description: Model id passed to the agent CLI.

tier.description: Tier name: lowercase letters, digits and dashes (not `inherit`).

oneOf.description: Deterministic stand-in used by tests and dry runs: no LLM, replays scripted responses. It accepts every tier name.

scriptDir.description: Directory (in the layer) holding <step>.json scripted responses and optional <step>.patch files.

artefacts.description: Proof a check or review produces. Collected from the worktree after the producing step and put in storage.

oneOf.description: Captured stdout/stderr of codebase commands (always available).

tailLines.description: Lines of each log shown to the reviewer.

oneOf.description: JUnit XML test report.
Coverage report (lcov, cobertura xml, or text).
Screenshots or rendered images; the reviewer reads every one.

maxFiles.description: Upper bound handed to the reviewer.

oneOf.description: Screen/session recordings; keyframes are extracted with ffmpeg for the reviewer.

keyframes.description: Evenly spaced frames extracted per video.

oneOf.description: Audio files (e.g. generated speech).
Tool traces such as Playwright trace.zip.
HTML reports.
Any other file worth keeping.

budget.description: Spending limits for agent work, in US dollars, counted from the cost each agent call reports (Claude Code reports it; codex and custom agents do not and count as $0). Omitted: no limits. A run that crosses a limit is stopped after the agent call that crossed it, never in the middle of one, and handed to a person like any other stopped run.

oneOf.description: Limits on what agent calls may cost. Each is optional; an omitted one is no limit.

dayUsd.description: Most this layer may spend per local calendar day, over all its runs. Once reached, no run and no agent step starts until the next day.

limitStopPercent.description: Subscription usage threshold, 1-100: once the agent CLI reports that this share of a usage window (Claude Code: the 5-hour or the weekly window) is used, no new agent step starts. 0 = off. Only applies when the CLI reports a share (a subscription login, not an API key).

limitWaitMinutes.description: Longest wait for a reset with #:on-limit wait, in minutes (at least 1).

onLimit.description: What happens at the threshold: `stop` = the run is handed to a person, with the window and its reset time as the reason; `wait` = the run waits until the window resets and then continues, unless that is further away than #:limit-wait-minutes (then it is handed over).

runUsd.description: Most one run may spend (the sum of its agent calls). A per-run `--max-cost USD` (or AL_MAX_COST) replaces it for that run.

stepUsd.description: Most one agent call may spend. With Claude Code the call is also capped natively (--max-budget-usd), so it stops early.

codebase.description: The application the layer wraps. Everything codebase-specific that templates need lives here.

items.description: A named shell command of the codebase: (cmd NAME "shell" …). Check steps and validation sections refer to these names.

always.description: #t = the command runs for every change. #f = where affected checks are asked for (a check step with #:when-affected #t, a gate with #:require affected) it runs only when a changed path is under its #:covers, and is recorded as not affected otherwise; needs #:covers.

coverageFile.description: File or directory, relative to the repository root, #:coverage-run writes the recipe's output to.

coverageRun.description: The full form with the runner's per-test coverage on, run instead of #:run when a full run records coverage.

covers.description: Paths this command proves something about, relative to the repository root: a directory ("kit/dashboard"), a file, or a glob ("*.md", "docs/**"). A cmd with #:covers is one of the layer's checks: (check NAME #:cmds affected) runs it, and `al verify` reports source paths no check covers.

maxTargeted.description: More tests selected than this: run the full form instead, and say so.

needsHome.description: The command needs state that exists only on the machine that holds the layer (a local database, a licence, a device): a workflow that runs it as a check or script is never placed on another host.

source.description: Source pattern relative to the repository root; {name} matches one file name without extension, {dir} one or more directories.

tests.description: Test glob relative to the repository root; {name} and {dir} are filled from the source.

recordCoverage.description: How a full run records which test executed which file: coverage-py = coverage.py JSON with contexts (coverage json --show-contexts); profile-dir = a directory with one lcov (.info) or Go cover profile per test, named after the test; al-json = al's own format. Needs #:coverage-run and #:coverage-file.

reuse.description: #t = a passing result is reused when the same command is asked for again on an identical tree in the same run (the gate after a passing check step, a review round that changed nothing). #f = it always runs again: for a command that is not deterministic.

run.description: Shell command, run from the worktree root.

select.description: Selection strategies, tried in this order and united: changed-tests = test files the change added or modified; path-map = #:path-map; imports = tests that import a changed module (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go packages, Rust crates); coverage = the map recorded by full runs (#:record-coverage); command = #:select-cmd. What earlier batch misses taught is always added.

selectCmd.description: For `command` in #:select: a shell command printing one test file or id per line; it gets AL_CHANGED (changed files, one per line) and AL_BASE (the commit compared against).

smoke.description: The smoke form: a few minutes, always meaningful (e.g. "pytest -q -m smoke"). Run at depth smoke, and at depth targeted when selection finds nothing for a covered change. "" = full instead.

targeted.description: The targeted form: the command run with the tests selected for a change, e.g. "pytest -q {tests}". Placeholders {tests} (selected test files or ids), {files} (changed files under #:covers), {packages} (Go packages as ./dir, Rust crates as names); at least one. "" = the command has only its full form (#:run).

testRoot.description: Directory, relative to the repository root, that {tests}, {files} and {packages} are relative to: the directory the command changes into ("kit/runtime" for "cd kit/runtime && pytest -q {tests}"). Selected paths outside it are dropped.

timeout.description: Seconds one run of the command may take; allow for several runs sharing the machine.

items.description: (conditional-doc "path" "condition" …): documentation an agent must read when the condition holds.

path.description: Document path relative to the codebase root.

description.description: One-paragraph description used by prime/plan templates.

packageManager.description: How dependencies are added (e.g. `uv add`, `cargo add`).

protected.description: Paths agents must not change without a human (CI config, release, security, migrations…).

root.description: Path of the application checkout, relative to the agentic.rkt file or absolute.

items.description: (command NAME #:template T …): instantiate a kit template as a command of this layer.

fabric.description: Fabric patterns vendored into the layer and applied by this command.

file.description: For template custom: path of a hand-written template relative to the layer.

focus.description: Codebase-specific instructions injected into the template's Instructions section.

mayCommit.description: Whether a run step of this command may commit (move HEAD in the worktree). The commit template always may; every other step's HEAD, refs and the layer directory are checked after it and a change fails the step.

modelSet.description: Model tier the command runs on: a tier declared on the agent that runs it (base, heavy, or one from #:models).

output.description: What the command must return: free text, JSON per its schema, or a file path.

relevant.description: Codebase paths listed under Relevant Files; empty = codebase source+tests paths.

validation.description: Codebase commands listed as Validation Commands.

concurrency.description: How far the layer scales out. Every run has its own worktree; these limits are shared by all triggers and manual runs.

oneOf.description: File-lock slot pools under agents/.slots: a run, an agent call and a check each hold one slot of their pool.

maxAgents.description: Agent (LLM) calls in flight at once across all runs.

maxChecks.description: Codebase check commands in flight at once across all runs (they are the CPU-heavy part).

maxRuns.description: ADW runs in flight at once (each in its own worktree).

waitSeconds.description: How long a run waits for a free slot before failing.

cycle.description: A stage that repeats: its branch is opened anew for each cycle (a sprint, a release). The current cycle is state of the layer (agents/cycle.json), changed with `al cycle LAYER status|start|close`.

oneOf.description: No stage repeats.
A time-boxed cycle (a sprint, a release train): a new branch every #:length-days days.

lengthDays.description: Days per cycle, 1–366; `al cycle status` reports when it is due.

name.description: Name of a cycle: {year}, {week} (ISO week), {n} (sequence number), {date} (YYYY-MM-DD).

stage.description: The stage whose branch repeats; its #:branch contains {cycle}.

oneOf.description: A cycle per version: a new branch when a release is started with `al cycle LAYER start --version V`.

name.description: Name of a cycle; must contain {version}.

stage.description: The stage whose branch repeats; its #:branch contains {cycle} or {version}.

dashboard.description: A live, read-only work dashboard for this layer (runs in flight, each run's workflow graph, timeline, costs, transcripts, check logs), generated by `al gen` as adws/dashboard.py. Declared by default: observability does not have to be asked for.

oneOf.description: A local process: `uv run adws/dashboard.py` serves the page (standard library only, no CDN) and watches this layer plus the #:also layers.

also.description: Other layer directories (relative to this layer, e.g. "../other.al") watched on the same page.

bind.description: Listen address. Anything other than a loopback address needs #:token-env.

pollMs.description: How often the run files are polled, in milliseconds (at least 100).

systemd.description: Also generate a systemd user unit (systemd/al-<name>-dashboard.service) that keeps it running.

tokenEnv.description: Environment variable holding an access token every request must carry; required for a non-loopback #:bind.

oneOf.description: The same dashboard in its own locked-down rootless podman container: layers mounted read-only, no capabilities, read-only root, an internal network with no route out, only 127.0.0.1:PORT published, a random token per start.

also.description: Other layer directories (relative to this layer) watched on the same page; mounted read-only too.

bind.description: Not used by the container, which publishes on 127.0.0.1 only; kept so that switching between `local` and `podman` is one word.

podmanSocket.description: Mount the user's podman API socket so the page can show container state, CPU and memory. Off by default for a reason: a podman socket gives the container full control of your podman (start, stop, exec into any container), read-only mount or not.

pollMs.description: How often the run files are polled, in milliseconds (at least 100).

systemd.description: Also generate a systemd user unit that keeps the container running.

tokenEnv.description: Not used by the container (it makes a random token per start and prints the URL with it).

oneOf.description: No dashboard is generated.

delivery.description: The (delivery PRESET …) clause: {preset, params, expansion (the clauses it stands for, one string each)}; null when stages are declared by hand only.

environments.description: PITER · Environment: where the agent works. An ADW lists one or more; they stack in order (worktree → nix → podman).

oneOf.description: The application checkout itself, no isolation. Only for read-only workflows.

readOnly.description: Refuse steps that are expected to write.

oneOf.description: A dedicated git worktree per run under the layer (trees/<adw-id>), so the app's working tree is never touched.

copyFiles.description: Untracked files copied from the app checkout into the worktree (e.g. .env).

deleteMergedBranches.description: When a run's worktree is removed, delete its branch if it holds nothing that is not already on the default or al/ship branch.

dir.description: Worktree parent directory relative to the layer.

gcDays.description: Kept worktrees of finished runs older than this are removed when a new run starts; 0 = never.

keep.description: When the worktree is kept after the run.

portBase.description: First port of the per-run port block.

portsPerRun.description: Ports reserved per run (exported as ADW_PORT_0..n).

prepare.description: Codebase cmds run once per run, in order, after the worktree exists and before the first step, in the run's environment (a container's caches are mounted): dependency installs such as `uv sync`, `bun install`, `cargo fetch`. Shown as a `setup` step; a failure ends the run with that output. With a podman #:devcontainer and no #:prepare, the dev container's postCreateCommand is the prepare step.

sparse.description: Sparse-checkout these directories only (cone mode); empty = full checkout. For large monorepos.

oneOf.description: A Nix flake dev shell generated in the layer; every codebase command and the agent run inside `nix develop`.

browser.description: Add a headless Chromium (Linux) and set AL_BROWSER and CHROME_BIN to it, for browser tests.

flake.description: Directory of the repository's own flake, relative to its root ("." = top level). Its dev shell #:shell is used (read from the default branch, refreshed at the start of every run); #:packages and #:browser are added on top. Empty = a shell generated from #:packages.

nixpkgs.description: nixpkgs flake reference (with #:packages only; a toolchain has its own).

packages.description: nixpkgs attribute names providing the toolchain (e.g. python312 uv); with #:flake, extras added on top of the repository's dev shell. Either this or #:toolchain.

pure.description: Use `nix develop --ignore-environment` (keeps HOME, PATH is nix-only).

shell.description: Name of the dev shell in the repository's flake (devShells.<system>.<name>). Only with #:flake.

toolchain.description: A declared (toolchain nix …) that provides the packages; either this or #:packages.

oneOf.description: A Home Manager module generated in the layer that installs the toolchain and the layer's helper commands for a user.

packages.description: nixpkgs attribute names. Either this or #:toolchain.

stateVersion.description: home.stateVersion used by the standalone example configuration.

toolchain.description: A declared (toolchain nix …) that provides the packages; either this or #:packages.

oneOf.description: A light rootless podman container; the worktree is bind-mounted, nothing else of the host is visible.

agentInside.description: Run the agent CLI inside the container, so the agent itself is sandboxed (the image must provide the agent CLI). #f = only the codebase commands (the checks) run inside; the agent then runs on the host with the user's own access.

browser.description: Install a headless Chromium in the image and set AL_BROWSER and CHROME_BIN.

caches.description: Named cache volumes shared across runs, mounted at /caches/NAME. Known names also set the tool's cache variable: uv, pip, cargo, go, npm, pre-commit.

containerfile.description: Path of the repository's own Containerfile or Dockerfile, relative to its root. The run builds it (from the run's worktree) as the base image; al adds only a thin final layer (run user home, #:packages, #:setup, #:browser, the agent CLI when #:agent-inside #t, no entrypoint). The repository's file is never edited.

context.description: Build context of #:containerfile, relative to the repository root. Only with #:containerfile.

credentials.description: Agent credentials made available inside the container (read-only auth file + API key variable). Only meaningful with #:agent-inside #t.

devcontainer.description: Path of the repository's dev container file (e.g. .devcontainer/devcontainer.json). Honoured: image or build (dockerfile, context, target), known features, containerEnv, postCreateCommand (as the prepare step), forwardPorts (as published ports). Everything else is listed in env/SOURCE.md and by al gen.

nestedEngine.description: Give the run's container a rootless podman of its own for tests that build or start containers. It stores everything in a per-run volume, cannot see the host's containers, images or socket, and stays inside the run's network and limits. Adds /dev/fuse to the container and nothing else: every capability stays dropped. One uid inside, so inner images that switch users do not work. The preflight refuses the run where the host cannot provide it.

network.description: Network mode: `slirp` = podman's default rootless user-mode network, `none` = fully offline checks, `host` = host network.

packages.description: Distribution packages installed in the image (apt names for Debian bases).

publish.description: Container ports published on 127.0.0.1 at the run's leased host ports, in order (first → ADW_PORT_0). Every run has its own network namespace, so the app inside always binds its usual ports and runs never collide; publish only what a host-side tool (browser, reviewer) must reach.

readOnlyRoot.description: Mount the image's root filesystem read-only; the worktree, caches, /tmp and the home directory stay writable.

scope.description: `run` = one container per ADW run, every step execs into it (installed dependencies persist for the run); `command` = a fresh container per command.

services.description: Sidecar services started with the run in the same pod (they share localhost with the run's container) and removed with it.

setup.description: Extra RUN lines for the Containerfile.

target.description: Build stage of #:containerfile (podman build --target). Only with #:containerfile.

toolchain.description: A declared (toolchain nix …): the image is built from it with Nix instead of from #:base-image and #:packages; #:setup lines are applied as a final layer.

items.description: (expert NAME …): an agent expert — an expertise file the agent maintains itself (act → learn → reuse).

domain.description: What the expert knows, in one sentence.

maxLines.description: Line cap of the expertise file.

paths.description: Codebase paths the expertise is validated against.

forge.description: The code forge used for issues, PRs and CI integration.

oneOf.description: No forge: branches stay local, review results are written to the layer.

remote.description: Optional git remote to push to.

oneOf.description: GitHub via the `gh` CLI.

botMarker.description: Prefix on every comment the layer posts, so triggers ignore their own comments.

tokenEnv.description: Environment variable holding the token (falls back to gh auth).

oneOf.description: Forgejo / Gitea via the REST API (v1).

botMarker.description: Prefix on every comment the layer posts.

tokenEnv.description: Environment variable holding the API token.

oneOf.description: GitLab via `glab`.

items.description: (hop NAME #:template T …): a higher-order prompt — it takes another prompt, plan or command as its argument.

modelSet.description: Model tier the HOP runs on (see command).

items.description: (host #:id ID …): what a machine that runs this layer must have, written with keywords only and declared once per kind of machine. From it `al gen` writes three committed provisioning files under the layer, env/hosts/<id>/home-manager.nix, env/hosts/<id>/nixos.nix and env/hosts/<id>/provision.sh, which hold no host name, user, address or secret: those are only known on the host. `al deploy --as ID --provision` shows the plan, asks once and applies it; `al deploy --status` lists the drift.

dashboardPort.description: Port of the dashboard on this machine; 0 = the layer's own (dashboard #:port).

fallbackBuild.description: When the image on the host was built from another env/Containerfile (its recipe hash differs): #t = untag it so the host builds at the first run; #f = stop the deploy.

id.description: Name of this kind of machine: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, no dots (it is not a host name). `al deploy --as ID` picks it.

images.description: Where the sandbox image comes from: `build` = the host builds it at the first run; `pull` = from the (registry …), as pushed by `al sandbox push`; `load` = streamed over the ssh connection by `al deploy`.

linger.description: Enable lingering, so the units keep running after the user logs out.

provision.description: How the machine is provisioned: `none` = al installs nothing and only checks; `home-manager` = a Home Manager module; `nixos` = a NixOS module (privileged rebuild); `script` = a POSIX shell script for Debian/Ubuntu, Fedora and Arch.

units.description: Units kept running on this machine; empty = every unit the layer declares.

layer.description: Where the generated agentic layer lives. Only `in-repo` puts it inside the application repository; the others keep it out of the application tree.

oneOf.description: A directory next to the application checkout (default: <app>.al).

dir.description: Layer directory; empty = `<codebase root>.al` beside the app.

git.description: Initialise the layer as its own git repository.

oneOf.description: A directory under a central layers home, e.g. ~/agentic-layers/<name>.

git.description: Initialise the layer as its own git repository.

oneOf.description: The layer is its own remote repository; the app is referenced by URL only.

remote.description: Git remote URL of the layer repository.

oneOf.description: The layer is a directory INSIDE the application repository, committed with the code. agentic.rkt lives in that directory and (codebase #:root …) is the way back up to the repository root (".." for a top-level directory). Run state (worktrees, run logs, artefacts, plans, the task list) stays in git-ignored directories of the layer, and every ADW that does not change the layer itself treats the layer directory as a protected path.

dir.description: Layer directory relative to the repository root (no `..`, no leading `/`).

notifiers.description: Tell a person when a run needs them or has ended. Each notifier lists the events it reports: `needs-human` (the run stopped and was handed to a person, including a spending or usage limit stop), `failed` (the run failed and nothing was handed over), `passed` (the run finished; nothing was merged by al), `shipped` (the run finished and its change was merged or deployed). A run reports exactly one of them, at most once per notifier, and a notifier that fails never fails the run. Nothing private is written here: an address, a server or a password is given as the NAME of an environment variable, whose value comes from the environment, from `local.env` in the layer directory (git-ignored, never committed) or from `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/al/<layer name>.env`. `al notify-test LAYER` sends a test message through every notifier.

oneOf.description: Nothing is sent.
An e-mail over SMTP (standard library only). The message is short: workflow, run id, what happened, where to look.

fromEnv.description: NAME of the environment variable holding the sender address. Never the address itself.

smtpUrlEnv.description: NAME of the environment variable holding the SMTP URL: `smtp://host:port` (plain; only to a loopback host, e.g. a local mail bridge, unless the URL ends in `?insecure=plaintext`), `smtp+starttls://user:pass@host:port` or `smtps://user:pass@host:port`. Never the URL itself.

timeout.description: Seconds one attempt may take, 1–60; after that the run goes on without it.

toEnv.description: NAME of the environment variable holding the recipient address (several: separated by commas). Never the address itself.

oneOf.description: Run a shell command with the message on standard input (first line: the subject). The generic way out: a chat webhook, a desktop notification, a pager. It runs in the layer directory with the variables of `local.env` in its environment, plus AL_NOTIFY_EVENT and AL_NOTIFY_SUBJECT; exit code 0 means accepted. Its output is discarded.

run.description: Shell command (sh -c). Refer to anything private as $VARIABLE; never write an address, a URL with a token or a password here.

timeout.description: Seconds one attempt may take, 1–60; after that the command is killed and the run goes on.

placement.description: Where runs of this layer may execute. Omitted: every run executes on the machine that holds the layer, as before. Hosts are `home` (a reserved id: the machine that holds the layer) or the ids of declared (host …) clauses. The address of a host is never written in the layer file: it comes from the variable AL_HOST_<ID> (the id in capitals, `-` as `_`) in the environment, in `local.env` in the layer directory or in `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/al/<layer name>.env`. A run on another host works in its own clone of the git source and can only push its own branch; the home machine fetches that branch and runs the workflow's (ship) step itself, through the unchanged gate.

oneOf.description: A scheduler on the home machine asks every listed host for its load, picks one by #:prefer and starts the run there. `al hosts LAYER status` shows what it sees; `al run LAYER /NAME … --on HOST` picks the host by hand.

hosts.description: Hosts runs may execute on, in declared order: `home` and/or ids of declared (host …) clauses.

layerSourceEnv.description: NAME of the variable holding the git source of a layer that is not in the application repository. Never the URL itself.

lostAfter.description: Seconds without an answer from a host after which its run is marked `lost`, 30–3600; `al run LAYER --restart RUN` starts it again on another host.

maxRunsPerHost.description: Runs in flight at once on each host, 1–64; replaces (concurrency #:max-runs) on every host including `home`. 0 = (concurrency #:max-runs) applies on each host.

prefer.description: `least-loaded`: the host with the lowest share of its runs in use (ties: the lower load average, then a host that already has the sandbox image, then the declared order); `first`: the first listed host with a free run.

reserve.description: Keep one host for some work classes, e.g. ((host build-2) (classes (chore bug))): that host only takes runs whose class is fixed at start to one of them.

classes.description: Work classes the host is kept for; at least one.

host.description: The reserved host: one of #:hosts, not `home`.

sourceEnv.description: NAME of the variable holding the git source: the URL runs clone the base commit from and push their own branch to (the forge's clone URL, or the home repository over ssh). Every machine holds its own value, the URL as seen from there. Never the URL itself.

items.description: (promotion FROM -> TO …): how a stage's work moves into the next stage — evidence for the people who accept it, a recorded decision, then merge, version, tag, deploy and back-merge. Run with `al promote LAYER FROM TO`; every non-final stage without one gets one with these defaults.

adw.description: Workflow whose environment, agent, review command and #:patch/#:implement commands the promotion's agent rounds use; "" = the first workflow that delivers into FROM, else the first workflow.

after.description: (deploy) or (deploy ENV): after merging, run TO's #:deploy-cmd; ENV must equal TO's #:environment-name.

approval.description: human: people approve (al decide, the dashboard, or an approving review / `/approve` on the pull request); agent: independent reviewer agents review the whole stage diff and the pack; auto: no approval. agent and auto only into a stage with #:agents-may-merge #t.

approvers.description: human: distinct people who must approve; agent: reviewer agents that must all pass. 1–9.

backMerge.description: Stages the promoted result is merged back into (an agent round resolves a conflict). A hotfix promotion (FROM is cut from TO) defaults to every other stage that accepts a class.

from.description: The stage whose branch is promoted.

hotfix.description: FROM is cut from the final stage TO and goes straight back into it (a hotfix): its own gate, merged back into the working stages.

origin.description: "declared" (a (promotion …) clause) or "default" (a non-final stage without one).

present.description: Sections of the presentation pack: summary, per-change details with acceptance criteria, proof (pictures, recordings), demo (one page to open and show), checks on the stage head, release notes and changelog entry, what is not included.

requires.description: checks: the #:checks of FROM and TO pass on the stage head; acceptance: every change is accepted or refused (or the whole promotion approved) before it merges.

tag.description: Tag on the promoted commit; placeholders {version} {cycle} {date}; "" = no tag.

to.description: The stage it goes into: FROM's #:into (default #:from).

version.description: The version change, e.g. (bump minor); none = the version is not touched.

how.description: bump: raise the version where the repository keeps it (VERSION, pyproject.toml, package.json, Cargo.toml; else the latest vX.Y.Z tag); keep: use the version it has.

promptInputs.description: PITER · Prompt input: where the high-level prompt for a run comes from.

oneOf.description: The prompt is passed on the command line (or stdin) of the ADW script.

allowStdin.description: Read the prompt from stdin when no argument is given.

oneOf.description: A forge issue (title + body). Requires a forge.

classify.description: Run the classify command to map the issue to chore/bug/feature.

keyword.description: Body/comment keyword prefix that selects a workflow and optionally a model tier, e.g. `adw: sdlc` or `adw: sdlc heavy` (any tier an agent of the layer declares).

labels.description: Only issues carrying all of these labels are picked up; empty = any.

oneOf.description: A plain-text task list (tasks.md) in the layer: one heading per worktree, one checkbox line per task.

blockedMarker.description: Marker of a task that waits for the tasks above it in the same section.

doneMarker.description: Marker written on success (followed by adw id and commit hash).

failedMarker.description: Marker written on failure (followed by adw id and reason).

openMarker.description: Marker of a task that is ready to be picked up.

path.description: Task file relative to the layer.

runningMarker.description: Marker written when an ADW claims the task (followed by the adw id).

tagSyntax.description: Tags select the workflow, the model tier (any tier an agent of the layer declares) and the class: `{sdlc, heavy}` or `#sdlc #heavy`.

oneOf.description: A hand-written spec/plan file dropped into a directory of the layer; planning is skipped.

dir.description: Directory relative to the layer that is watched for new specs.

pattern.description: Glob of files treated as specs.

oneOf.description: Speak the prompt: local recording → speech recognition → text. Requires a `voice` declaration.

appendToTasklist.description: When routed as task, append to the tasklist instead of running immediately.

confirm.description: Read the recognised prompt back and wait for a spoken/typed yes before running.

route.description: What speech becomes: a new tasklist entry, a codebase question, a status summary, or classified automatically.

oneOf.description: A JSON payload posted to the webhook trigger by any external system.

promptField.description: Dotted path of the prompt text in the payload.

workflowField.description: Dotted path of the workflow (ADW) name in the payload.

oneOf.description: A Notion database row (status Not started → In progress → Done).

databaseIdEnv.description: Environment variable with the database id.

oneOf.description: A chat message (Telegram / Slack / Matrix).

tokenEnv.description: Environment variable with the bot token.

oneOf.description: (registry #:address-env VAR …): the container registry `al sandbox push|pull` and hosts with #:images pull use. It holds only the NAMES of environment variables, whose values come from the environment, `local.env` in the layer or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/al/<layer name>.env`. Declared at most once.

addressEnv.description: NAME of the variable holding the registry address and repository prefix, e.g. registry.example.org/team. Never the address itself.

passwordEnv.description: NAME of the variable holding the registry password or token; given together with #:username-env.

usernameEnv.description: NAME of the variable holding the registry user; empty = no login.

reviews.description: PITER · Review: how the result is judged and what happens after.

oneOf.description: Open a pull request and stop. A human reads it (presence = 2: prompt and review).

bodyCmd.description: Codebase command run in the worktree just before the pull request is written; its standard output (markdown) opens the PR description. It gets ADW_STATE (path of the run's state.json) and ADW_BASE (the commit the change is based on).

oneOf.description: An agent reviews the diff against the spec, with artefacts as proof, and posts a structured verdict. A human still merges.

agent.description: Agent the reviewer steps run on; empty = the workflow's agent. A different agent here (another vendor or model) reviews the first one's work. The patch and implement steps of a review round stay on the workflow's agent.

bodyCmd.description: Codebase command whose standard output opens the PR description (see review human).

maxRetries.description: Patch-and-re-review attempts on blockers before stopping for a human.

reviewers.description: Independent review agents; all must pass ('double agent check').

oneOf.description: Zero-touch: agent review + deterministic gates; if everything passes the change ships without a human.

agent.description: Agent the reviewer steps run on; empty = the workflow's agent (see review agent).

allowedClasses.description: Work classes allowed to ship untouched; others fall back to a human PR.

artefacts.description: Artefacts collected, stored and given to the reviewer as proof.

blockProtectedPaths.description: Any change under codebase protected paths falls back to a human PR.

bodyCmd.description: Codebase command whose standard output opens the PR description (see review human).

deployCmd.description: Codebase command run after merge when ship = deploy.

maxDiffLines.description: Larger diffs fall back to a human PR.

require.description: all = every #:require-checks cmd has a passing result for the exact tree that ships (run at the gate, or reused from the same tree). affected = a required cmd with #:always #f whose #:covers no changed path touches is recorded as not affected instead; the compiler warns when this is combined with #:ship merge or deploy.

requireChecks.description: Codebase commands that must exit 0 in the final state (the deterministic gate).

reviewers.description: Independent review agents; all must pass.

ship.description: On pass: open PR only, merge to the default branch, or merge and run the deploy command.

services.description: Per-run sidecar services (database, cache, mock API). Each run gets its own instances, so parallel runs never share state.

oneOf.description: A container started in the run's pod before the first step and removed with the run.

command.description: Command override; empty = the image's default.

readyCmd.description: Command run inside the sidecar until it exits 0 (e.g. `pg_isready -U postgres`); empty = no wait.

items.description: (stage NAME #:branch "…" …): a named place where work accumulates.

accepts.description: Work classes routed here by default (the first declared stage that accepts a class gets it).

agentsMayMerge.description: Whether a zero-touch workflow may merge into it; #f = only people change it (runs end in a pull request).

branch.description: Branch name or pattern; placeholders {cycle} and {version} (only on the cycle's stage) and {date} (the cycle's opening date on the cycle's stage, else the run's UTC start date).

checks.description: Codebase cmds that must hold on it: added to the review's #:require-checks for runs delivering here.

deployCmd.description: Codebase cmd that deploys this stage; used by a review with #:ship deploy that has no #:deploy-cmd of its own.

environmentName.description: Where the deploy lands, in words (e.g. staging, production); shown in the run summary and by al explain.

from.description: Stage this one is cut from; "" = none (the final stage).

frozen.description: Periods closed to new deliveries, each "YYYY-MM-DD..YYYY-MM-DD" (UTC, both days included): a run that would deliver then ends `waiting` at its deliver step and says until when.

frozenWhilePromoting.description: Closed to new deliveries while a promotion out of this stage is open.

into.description: Stage it is delivered into when accepted; "" = #:from.

origin.description: "declared", or "preset NAME" for a stage a (delivery …) preset made.

standIn.description: A stand-in for the person a run waits for: a strong model reads what the person would read and decides, inside the scope declared here. Omitted: off, and a person may still switch it on for this machine with `al decider` or the dashboard, where it may then only resume a stopped run. It never overrides a rejected review, never lands work with a protected-path change or a failing required check, never approves its own work, never edits code and never acts on a run a person touched since it stopped; `land` and `promote` only ask the gate again.

oneOf.description: Declared, and off until a person switches it on on this machine.

escalateTo.description: Where an item goes when it hands it to a person: `dashboard` = the Needs you list; `notify` = also a message through the notifiers that list needs-human.

maxActionsPerRun.description: Most actions it takes on one run (and the runs that replace it), 1–20; after that the run goes to a person with the history.

maxPerHour.description: Most actions it takes in this layer per hour, 1–1000.

may.description: Decision kinds it may take alone (kind auto). Every other kind it may only suggest.

modelSet.description: Model tier of the stand-in's calls: a tier declared on the agent of every ADW.

never.description: Decision kinds it neither takes nor suggests: those items go to a person as they are.

systemd.description: Also generate a systemd user unit (systemd/al-<name>-stand-in.service) that keeps its loop running without the page.

oneOf.description: It proposes; a person answers on the dashboard, with `al answer`, by mail or by webhook.

escalateTo.description: Where an item goes when it hands it to a person: `dashboard` = the Needs you list; `notify` = also a message through the notifiers that list needs-human.

maxActionsPerRun.description: Most actions it takes on one run (and the runs that replace it), 1–20; after that the run goes to a person with the history.

maxPerHour.description: Most actions it takes in this layer per hour, 1–1000.

may.description: Decision kinds it may take alone (kind auto). Every other kind it may only suggest.

modelSet.description: Model tier of the stand-in's calls: a tier declared on the agent of every ADW.

never.description: Decision kinds it neither takes nor suggests: those items go to a person as they are.

systemd.description: Also generate a systemd user unit (systemd/al-<name>-stand-in.service) that keeps its loop running without the page.

oneOf.description: It takes the decisions listed in #:may by itself and proposes the others.

escalateTo.description: Where an item goes when it hands it to a person: `dashboard` = the Needs you list; `notify` = also a message through the notifiers that list needs-human.

maxActionsPerRun.description: Most actions it takes on one run (and the runs that replace it), 1–20; after that the run goes to a person with the history.

maxPerHour.description: Most actions it takes in this layer per hour, 1–1000.

may.description: Decision kinds it may take alone (kind auto). Every other kind it may only suggest.

modelSet.description: Model tier of the stand-in's calls: a tier declared on the agent of every ADW.

never.description: Decision kinds it neither takes nor suggests: those items go to a person as they are.

systemd.description: Also generate a systemd user unit (systemd/al-<name>-stand-in.service) that keeps its loop running without the page.

storage.description: Where test/review artefacts (logs, reports, screenshots, video) are kept. Local first.

oneOf.description: Artefacts stay on disk inside the layer.
Any S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, MinIO, Cloudflare R2, Garage). A local copy is always kept too.

accessKeyEnv.description: Environment variable with the access key.

endpoint.description: Endpoint URL for non-AWS stores; empty = AWS.

localDir.description: Local mirror directory relative to the layer.

publicBaseUrl.description: If set, artefact links in reviews use this base URL.

secretKeyEnv.description: Environment variable with the secret key.

testing.description: (testing DEPTH #:k v …): how deep a run's checks go and how the whole is proven per batch. Declared at most once; without it every check runs its full form (the layer predates targeted testing). Depths: targeted (the tests a change concerns), full (whole suites), smoke (each cmd's #:smoke). #:escalate ((paths "G" …) (diff-lines N) (files N) (lockfile) (layer) (unmapped) (class C …)) and #:batch ((every N) (after-hours H)) are written as lists and stand for the escalate-… and batch-… fields.

batchAfterHours.description: Run a batch when a change landed and the last batch is older than this many hours; 0 = not by time.

batchEvery.description: Run a batch after this many changes landed on a branch since its last batch; 0 = not by count.

depth.description: The layer's depth: the default of #:per-run and #:review-rounds.

escalateClasses.description: Work classes that always run at full depth.

escalateDiffLines.description: A change of more lines than this runs at full depth; 0 = no limit.

escalateFiles.description: A change of more files than this runs at full depth; 0 = no limit.

escalateOn.description: lockfile = a dependency manifest or lock file changed; layer = the agentic layer changed; unmapped = a changed path under a cmd's #:covers that no selection strategy could map to a test.

escalatePaths.description: Core areas: a changed path matching one of these globs runs this run at full depth.

fixAdw.description: Workflow a fix run uses; "" = the first workflow that accepts class bug.

maxMissPercent.description: A command whose miss rate over its last 50 batch-verified targeted runs exceeds this falls back to full and says so; 0 = never.

onBatchFailure.description: bisect = find the delivered run that broke the batch (failing tests only, on the commits since the last green batch); open-fix = start a fix run with the failing tests, the culprit and its plan; revert = prepare a revert branch, and ask the fix run to revert where agents may merge.

onStage.description: Depth of a batch: on a stage head (cycle closed, before a promotion is offered, the batch rhythm) and on the default branch.

perRun.description: Depth of a run's check steps and its gate; inherit = DEPTH.

reviewRounds.description: Depth of the re-checks of a review round, selected from what the patch touched; inherit = DEPTH.

toolchains.description: The tools a layer's environments provide, declared once and pinned with Nix: `(environment nix-devshell #:toolchain ID)`, `(environment podman #:toolchain ID …)` and `(environment home-manager #:toolchain ID)` all take exactly this set from one generated file, env/toolchain-<id>.nix. `al gen` pins nixpkgs in env/flake.lock (committed); `al sandbox LAYER update` re-pins it and `al sandbox LAYER build` builds the sandbox image when the lock or the declaration changed.

oneOf.description: A set of nixpkgs packages plus ready-made feature bundles, from one pinned nixpkgs. For a podman environment the image is built from it with Nix (on the host, or in a builder container pinned by digest when the host has no Nix).

agentClis.description: Derived: the agent kinds (sorted, without mock) whose workflows run their agent inside an environment using this toolchain; feature agent-cli provides their CLIs.

items.description: One environment variable of a toolchain, written ("NAME" "VALUE") inside #:env.

name.description: Variable name: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit.

features.description: Ready-made bundles; see `Toolchain features` below for what each adds.

nixpkgs.description: nixpkgs flake reference; env/flake.lock pins its exact revision.

shellHook.description: Extra shell hook of the dev shell.

triggers.description: PITER · Trigger: the event that starts a run.

oneOf.description: Run the ADW script by hand: `adws/adw_<name>.py <prompt-or-ref>`.
A polling loop (uv script, optionally a systemd user timer) that checks the prompt inputs.

systemd.description: Also generate a systemd user service + timer unit.

oneOf.description: A small HTTP server receiving forge webhooks or generic JSON payloads.

bind.description: Bind address; put a tunnel/reverse proxy in front for remote forges.

secretEnv.description: Environment variable with the HMAC secret.

oneOf.description: A CI workflow file for the forge (GitHub Actions / Forgejo Actions) that runs the ADW on a runner.

label.description: Issue label that must be present for issue events.

runner.description: runs-on label. A self-hosted runner keeps the agent on hardware you control.

schedule.description: Cron expression when `schedule` is among the events.

oneOf.description: Watch a file or directory in the layer (tasklist, spec inbox) and start when it changes.

debounceSeconds.description: Quiet period before a change is acted on.

oneOf.description: Push-to-talk loop: press Enter, speak, the recognised text is routed by the voice prompt input.

hotkey.description: Key that starts recording in the terminal loop.

voice.description: Local speech stack used by the voice prompt input and trigger, and for spoken summaries.

oneOf.description: Kokoro TTS (ONNX, local, English) + faster-whisper speech recognition, both as uv scripts.

dashboardHelper.description: Show the voice helper panel on the dashboard: talk about this layer's runs; it proposes work, and a person starts it with a click on Approve.

helperAgent.description: Agent id the helper thinks with; empty = the first declared agent. It must be claude-code or mock, which run with no tools.

helperModelSet.description: Model tier of the helper's agent.

interrupt.description: In always-listen mode, speaking over the helper stops its playback.

listenMode.description: The panel's listening mode until a person switches it (remembered per browser): `hold` to talk, or `always` listen with voice-activity detection.

maxUtteranceSeconds.description: Longest utterance that is recognised, 5–120 seconds.

recordSeconds.description: Push-to-talk recording length when no silence detection is available.

speakSummaries.description: Speak the run summary when an ADW finishes.
